question.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{2}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $4$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $3$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4}^{8}\frac{1}{x{log}_{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{4}^{8}\frac{1}{{log}_{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2{\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2(\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|){|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\operatorname{ln}⁡\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
